faq.q: Is False Creek a City of Vancouver local area?
faq.a: No — the City's 22 local areas treat it in parts: False Creek North inside Downtown, False Creek South inside Fairview, and the False Creek Flats at the east end in Strathcona; "False Creek" is the Paragon sub-area name spanning all three.

faq.q: Where exactly is False Creek South, and what is the land tenure there?
faq.a: Between the Cambie and Burrard Street bridges on the south shore, excluding Granville Island and Sen̓áḵw; the City holds title to 80 acres there and most homes sit on 60-year ground leases expiring in the next 15 to 25 years.

faq.q: Which schools are located around False Creek?
faq.a: Crosstown šxʷwəq̓ʷəθət Elementary, 55 Expo Boulevard, and Elsie Roy Elementary, 150 Drake Street, on the north shore, and False Creek Elementary, 900 School Green, on the south shore; no shoreline secondary school was confirmed, and catchments are address-based and differ by shore — check the exact address in the VSB locator.

faq.q: Is flooding a real factor for False Creek homes?
faq.a: Yes — the False Creek area is inside the City's designated floodplain system, the Coastal Adaptation Plan covers the False Creek floodplain (North, South, Granville Island and the Flats), and parcels in the floodplain carry Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements; a specific parcel's status must be checked in the City dataset.

faq.q: What transit serves the south shore and Granville Island?
faq.a: TransLink route 50 runs from Waterfront Station via Chinatown, Granville Island and the False Creek south shore to Olympic Village Station on the Canada Line, with buses continuing as route 15.
